name: Ahornbahn
kurzbeschreibung: The Ahornbahn in Mayrhofen, Zillertal, is Austria's largest reversible aerial tramway, whisking visitors in 160-passenger cabins to the panoramic Ahorn leisure plateau.
preis: Lift tickets apply (discounts available with regional guest cards)
oeffnungszeiten: Summer operation daily mid-June to late October
beschreibung:
Überblick

The Ahornbahn in Mayrhofen, situated in the heart of the Zillertal Valley, ranks as a landmark of modern ropeway engineering and proudly stands as Austria's largest reversible aerial tramway. Featuring two distinctive, red double-decker cabins that each hold up to 160 passengers, the tram ascends smoothly in just six and a half minutes from the valley base in Mayrhofen (670 m) to the sweeping Ahorn plateau at an altitude of 1,966 metres. Celebrated as the 'Leisure Mountain' (Genießerberg), Mount Ahorn offers a serene and nature-focused counterpoint to the vibrant mountain sports on neighboring Mount Penken. Upon reaching the top terminal, guests step out onto a sprawling high-alpine plateau boasting panoramic vistas across the glaciated 3,000-metre peaks of the Zillertal Alps, the Tux Ridge, and the rugged Stilluptal. Prominent attractions include the tranquil Lake Ahornsee, the family-friendly Ahornbachl stream, sensory barefoot paths, and the Adlerbühne Ahorn—Europe's highest bird of prey sanctuary.

Route & Anforderungen

The Ahorn plateau is tailored to pleasure walkers, multi-generational families, and dedicated alpinists alike. Surrounding the cable car top terminal is the barrier-free Panorama Trail (Genießerrundweg), engineered with smooth gravel walkways, oversized wooden relaxation loungers, and cantilevered viewing platforms offering dizzying views into the Zillertal and Stilluptal valleys. Along the babbling waters of the Ahornbachl stream, children can construct pebble dams and play with interactive waterwheels, while parents unwind alongside Lake Ahornsee. More ambitious mountaineers can embark on challenging summit ascents, such as the trek up the rocky Ahornspitze (2,973 m, roughly 3 hours uphill from the cable car station, requiring surefootedness and a head for heights on boulder terrain) or the hike to the alpine Karl-von-Edel-Hütte (1.5 hours). Comfortable walking shoes are sufficient for the plateau trail, whereas sturdy vibram-soled mountain boots are necessary for higher rocky trails.

Besuch & Anreise

The base station of the Ahornbahn is conveniently situated on the southern outskirts of Mayrhofen. Motorists arrive via the Inntal motorway A12 (exit Zillertal) and drive south along federal highway B169 straight to Mayrhofen. Spacious free parking lots and covered spaces are available directly beside the valley terminal. Public transport connections are excellent: visitors ride the scenic Zillertalbahn narrow-gauge railway from Jenbach mainline station to Mayrhofen terminal, and then connect to the free local green shuttle bus or walk 15 minutes along the village promenade.

Tipps

Do not miss the spectacular falconry demonstration at the Adlerbühne Ahorn at 2,000 metres elevation. Daily except Fridays, master falconers showcase majestic golden eagles, buzzards, and eagle owls soaring effortlessly against the jagged high-alpine skyline. In midsummer, early bird lift tickets allow guests to experience breathtaking mountaintop sunrises followed by a hearty alpine breakfast on sun-drenched lodge terraces.
